lines.raw: What is a provider?
lines.say: What is a provider?

lines.raw: A **provider** is any person or organisation that **gives** healthcare.
lines.say: A provider is any person or organisation that gives healthcare.

lines.raw: Doctors, nurses, hospitals, clinics, labs and pharmacies are all providers.
lines.say: Doctors, nurses, hospitals, clinics, labs and pharmacies are all providers.

lines.raw: Providers do the work, then send a bill (a **claim**) to get paid.
lines.say: Providers do the work, then send a bill (a claim) to get paid.

lines.raw: Common kinds of providers.
lines.say: Common kinds of providers.

lines.raw: **Primary care doctor (PCP)**. What they do: First doctor for everyday problems and check-ups. Nepal example: The general physician you see in OPD. US example in our story: Dr. Patel, Emily's family doctor.
lines.say: Primary care doctor (P C P). What they do: First doctor for everyday problems and check-ups. Nepal example: The general physician you see in O P D. U S example in our story: Doctor Patel, Emily's family doctor.

lines.raw: **Specialist**. What they do: Expert in one area: heart, skin, surgery and so on. Nepal example: A cardiologist at Shahid Gangalal or a surgeon at a big hospital. US example in our story: Dr. Lee, surgeon at Lakeside Surgical Group.
lines.say: Specialist. What they do: Expert in one area: heart, skin, surgery and so on. Nepal example: A cardiologist at Shahid Gangalal or a surgeon at a big hospital. U S example in our story: Doctor Lee, surgeon at Lakeside Surgical Group.

lines.raw: **Hospital**. What they do: Stays overnight, surgery, emergency care. Nepal example: Bir Hospital, Teaching Hospital, private hospitals. US example in our story: Lakeside General Hospital.
lines.say: Hospital. What they do: Stays overnight, surgery, emergency care. Nepal example: Bir Hospital, Teaching Hospital, private hospitals. U S example in our story: Lakeside General Hospital.

lines.raw: **Clinic / outpatient centre**. What they do: Visits and small procedures, no overnight stay. Nepal example: A polyclinic in your neighbourhood. US example in our story: Sunrise Family Clinic, where Dr. Patel works.
lines.say: Clinic or outpatient centre. What they do: Visits and small procedures, no overnight stay. Nepal example: A polyclinic in your neighbourhood. U S example in our story: Sunrise Family Clinic, where Doctor Patel works.

lines.raw: **Laboratory**. What they do: Blood tests, swabs, other tests. Nepal example: A diagnostic centre where you collect reports next day. US example in our story: A lab that tests a blood sample.
lines.say: Laboratory. What they do: Blood tests, swabs, other tests. Nepal example: A diagnostic centre where you collect reports next day. U S example in our story: A lab that tests a blood sample.

lines.raw: **Pharmacy**. What they do: Gives out prescribed medicines. Nepal example: A medical shop / pharmacy. US example in our story: Main Street Pharmacy.
lines.say: Pharmacy. What they do: Gives out prescribed medicines. Nepal example: A medical shop or pharmacy. U S example in our story: Main Street Pharmacy.

lines.raw: All names in our story are made up.
lines.say: All names in our story are made up.

lines.raw: Dr. Patel, Dr. Lee, Dr. Gomez, Sunrise Family Clinic, Lakeside General Hospital and Main Street Pharmacy are **fictional**, used only for learning.
lines.say: Doctor Patel, Doctor Lee, Doctor Gomez, Sunrise Family Clinic, Lakeside General Hospital and Main Street Pharmacy are fictional, used only for learning.

lines.raw: Primary care vs specialist.
lines.say: Primary care versus specialist.

lines.raw: In the US, most people have a **primary care physician (PCP)**: a family doctor, internal medicine doctor or paediatrician who knows their history.
lines.say: In the U S, most people have a primary care physician (P C P): a family doctor, internal medicine doctor or paediatrician who knows their history.

lines.raw: The PCP handles everyday problems and sends the patient to a **specialist** when needed.
lines.say: The P C P handles everyday problems and sends the patient to a specialist when needed.

lines.raw: This sending is called a **referral**.
lines.say: This sending is called a referral.

lines.raw: In Nepal: Going straight to the specialist.
lines.say: In Nepal: Going straight to the specialist.

lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: In Nepal, Ram can usually walk into a big hospital and book a ticket to see a specialist directly.
lines.say: In Nepal, Ram can usually walk into a big hospital and book a ticket to see a specialist directly.

lines.raw: Nobody asks for a referral letter.
lines.say: Nobody asks for a referral letter.

lines.say: The same day, she collects amoxicillin at Main Street Pharmacy.

scenes.section: Where to go when you are sick

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Doctor's office** (PCP). Use it for: Check-ups, fever, ongoing conditions. Rough cost to the plan: Lowest.
lines.say: Doctor's office (P C P). Use it for: Check-ups, fever, ongoing conditions. Rough cost to the plan: Lowest.

lines.raw: **Urgent care centre**. Use it for: Needs care today, but not life-threatening: a sprain, a cut. Rough cost to the plan: Medium.
lines.say: Urgent care centre. Use it for: Needs care today, but not life-threatening: a sprain, a cut. Rough cost to the plan: Medium.

lines.raw: **Emergency room (ER)**. Use it for: Serious and sudden: chest pain, a bad accident, appendicitis. Rough cost to the plan: Highest.
lines.say: Emergency room (E R). Use it for: Serious and sudden: chest pain, a bad accident, appendicitis. Rough cost to the plan: Highest.

lines.say: In network and out of network.

scenes.section: In network and out of network

lines.raw: Insurance companies sign **contracts** with providers.
lines.say: Insurance companies sign contracts with providers.

lines.raw: In the contract, the provider agrees to accept a set price (the **allowed amount**) for each service.
lines.say: In the contract, the provider agrees to accept a set price (the allowed amount) for each service.

lines.raw: Providers with a contract are **in network**.
lines.say: Providers with a contract are in network.

lines.raw: Providers without one are **out of network**.
lines.say: Providers without one are out of network.

scenes.section: In network and out of network

lines.raw: Like a hotel with a corporate rate.
lines.say: Like a hotel with a corporate rate.

lines.raw: A company in Kathmandu agrees a special room rate with certain hotels for its staff.
lines.say: A company in Kathmandu agrees a special room rate with certain hotels for its staff.

lines.raw: Staff who stay at those hotels pay the lower agreed rate.
lines.say: Staff who stay at those hotels pay the lower agreed rate.

lines.raw: Staff who stay elsewhere pay the full price, and the company may refund only part of it.
lines.say: Staff who stay elsewhere pay the full price, and the company may refund only part of it.

lines.raw: Insurance networks work the same way.
lines.say: Insurance networks work the same way.

lines.raw: Why network matters for Emily.
lines.say: Why network matters for Emily.

lines.raw: Price. In network: Contracted **allowed amount** (lower). Out of network: Often the full **billed** price.
lines.say: Price. In network: Contracted allowed amount (lower). Out of network: Often the full billed price.

lines.raw: Emily's share. In network: Her normal copay or coinsurance. Out of network: Usually more, and some plans pay nothing.
lines.say: Emily's share. In network: Her normal copay or coinsurance. Out of network: Usually more, and some plans pay nothing.

lines.raw: Who sends the claim? In network: The provider, directly to the insurer. Out of network: Usually the provider, but sometimes Emily pays and claims it back herself, like Ram.
lines.say: Who sends the claim? In network: The provider, directly to the insurer. Out of network: Usually the provider, but sometimes Emily pays and claims it back herself, like Ram.

lines.raw: See the discount in action.
lines.say: See the discount in action.

lines.raw: Dr. Patel **billed $150** for Emily's visit, but because she is in network, the insurer's **allowed amount** is only **$102**.
lines.say: Doctor Patel billed 150 dollars for Emily's visit, but because she is in network, the insurer's allowed amount is only 102 dollars.

lines.raw: The $48 difference ($150 - $102) is a contract discount: nobody pays it.
lines.say: The 48 dollars difference (150 dollars - 102 dollars) is a contract discount: nobody pays it.
